messages.subject: Contributing in "Integration of Text Mining and Topic Modeling Tools"
parts:
Hi!

I am Shubhankar Srivastava, Third Year Undergraduate in CS from BITS Pilani, India.

I'm highly motivated to work in NLP and ML, and would like to start contributing to the project "Integration of Text Mining and Topic Modeling Tools" for GSoc '16. 

I have previous experience with using LDA on various occasions for social media posts (Twitter/Instagram) clustering. I've also played with visualizations with the LDAvis package in R. Proficiency in R and the "tm" package specifically, would help me a great deal in contributing to this project. 

Since the "Tests" section of the idea proposal majorly lists familiarity with R/ML Tools, I was wondering how I could contribute to the project directly.

Any feedback/suggestions are welcome!

Thanks!

Thanks,

Can you write a supervised tool in R for creating alternative multilingual topic models for use in the the Wikipedia Disaster Monitor, covering subjects other than disasters, e.g., occupations, general interests, or locales? Wikipedia has built-in term translations and several means of deriving topic term categories which helped construct the dIsaster monitor.

Please see: http://disaster-monitor.herokuapp.com
-- source code:
http://github.com/tomayac/postdoc/tree/master/demos/disaster-monitor
-- papers: http://ceur-ws.org/Vol-1268/paper15.pdf and
http://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.06329v1.pdf etc.
-- slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1b563mkeP91PMWJ6B_Fy3DdKK-SjM06gPVNu2s1uAxBk/edit#slide=id.i0

Please ask Macej Eder and Islam Tolan if they are interested in co-mentoring such a project. Last year Islam was interested in similar work. I have copied them both on this email.

Best regards,
Jim
